segments.t: We have moderated our equity position. We've reduced AI exposure in favor of lower volatility names with an emphasis on
consistent fundamentals. Russ joins us now for more. Russ, welcome to the program, sir. That wall of equity supplies, is that a
factor in any of this? Well, I think the supply is actually less of an issue versus what has happened over the last three or
four months. You know, we do have supply, but the reality is buybacks have also been very high and relative to market cap. The
supply is modest compared to some of the years we saw back in the late nineties. But what I do think the market is still
working through is the unwinding of that massive momentum trade that built up in the first half of the year. We know the
beneficiaries was AI, was semiconductors, was memory. So a lot of money come into that space. A lot of leverage come into
that space. And that has been a multi-month unwind they think we're still in the middle of. The fundamentals actually
look solid, but it is the technicals that's causing us to pull back a little bit on risk right now. Russ, it's not just chips.
It's copper, too. Chips have been hammered. Cop has been hammered. We've talked a little bit about the curve flattening
we've seen more recently as well through the Treasury curve. And this Fed is willing to keep on hiking. Do you think we
are facing the prospect? I'm not saying on the same scale, but facing the prospect of a move like we saw in 22 in this
equity market. I don't think so. And the reason is we have a much more modest inflation problem than we did in
two thousand twenty two, where, you know, as you know, inflation peaked out at nine percent. The Fed embarked on
this most aggressive tightening campaign in 40 years. I don't think that's what we're looking at. Clearly, the Fed
pivoting from easing to hiking has tripped up the market a bit. But the reality is we get another two or three hikes.
That happens in the context of a strong economy where nominal GDP is let's call it six percent. It's supporting double
digit earnings. I think the market can withstand that much easier than the situation.
